pairs.semantic_rationale: GB020 asks for presence of definite/specific article; WALS 37A value includes only dedicated definite articles distinct from demonstratives. Near-exact: GB020=1 also covers 'demonstrative used as article' (a separate WALS 37A value), so GB020=1 is slightly broader.

pairs.wals_value_label: Demonstrative word used as definite article
pairs.semantic_rationale: Both mark a definite/specific article strategy. GB020=1 covers this case explicitly; WALS has it as a separate value.
Both WALS 37A 'No article' and GB020=0 assert absence of any definite/specific article. Near-exact; minor scope differences in what counts as an article.
GB021 asks whether indefinite/non-specific nominals commonly have indefinite articles. WALS 38A value is the same scope. GB021 explicitly cites WALS 38.
Both assert no indefinite article.
Presence of only definite article entails absence of indefinite article (GB021=0).

GB024=1 codes numeral before noun; WALS 89A 'Numeral precedes noun' is the same condition. Near-exact rather than exact because WALS 89A includes a 'numeral only modifies verb' value with no GB024 equivalent. GB024 cites WALS chapter 89.
GB024=2 codes numeral after noun; WALS 89A 'Noun precedes numeral' is the same condition. Same caveat as above.

Both GB025=1 and WALS 88A code demonstrative-before-noun for adnominal demonstratives. Near-exact for free demonstratives; WALS 88A also includes separate affixal values with no GB025 equivalent. GB025 cites WALS chapter 88.
Same as above for the post-nominal value.

GB065=1 codes possessor-before-possessed; WALS 86A 'Genitive precedes noun' is the same condition. Both focus on the pragmatically unmarked order. Minor caveat: WALS uses 'dominant' and GB uses 'pragmatically unmarked'.
Same as above for post-nominal possessor.
GB193=1 codes adnominal property word before noun; WALS 87A codes adjective before noun. Near-exact; WALS terminology is 'adjective' while GB uses 'adnominal property word'.
Same as above, post-nominal adjective/property word.

WALS 85A 'Prepositions' means prepositions are the dominant adposition type. GB074=1 means prepositions are present. WALS dominance implies GB presence, but not vice versa: a language may have prepositions (GB074=1) while its dominant adposition type is postpositions (WALS 85A=Postpositions). Directional: WALS 85A=Prep ⇒ GB074=1.
Same directional logic as for prepositions. WALS 85A=Postp ⇒ GB075=1.
WALS 85A 'No adpositions' means neither prepositions nor postpositions exist. GB074=0 & GB075=0 expresses the same condition directly. Near-exact.
WALS 82A 'SV' codes subject-before-verb as dominant order in intransitive clauses. GB130=1 codes the same. Near-exact; minor dominance vs. pragmatic-unmarkedness framing difference.
WALS 82A 'VS' and GB130=2 both code verb-before-subject intransitive order.
WALS 83A 'OV' includes both SOV and OSV orders. GB133=1 codes verb-final transitive order. WALS OV ⇒ GB133=1, but GB133=1 also collapses OSV. Directional projection.
WALS 90A 'Noun precedes RC' and GB327=1 ('can RC follow noun?') both assert postposed relative clauses. Near-exact.
WALS 90A 'RC precedes noun' and GB328=1 both assert preposed relative clauses.
Both directly code internally headed relative clauses.
Both directly code correlative relative clauses.
Both assert absence of grammatical evidentiality. Near-exact; minor scope differences in what counts as grammatical evidential.
WALS 77A 'Indirect only' and GB323=1 (indirect evidential present) directly correspond. Near-exact.
WALS 77A 'Direct and indirect' implies GB322=1 (direct evidential present). Near-exact; GB322 does not require indirect to also be present.
WALS 67A 'Inflectional future' and GB084=1 ('overt morphological future tense') directly correspond.
Both assert absence of dedicated inflectional future morphology.
WALS 79A 'Tense and aspect suppletion' maps to GB110=1 ('verb suppletion for tense or aspect'). Near-exact; GB110 uses 'or' while WALS value specifies 'and', so GB110=1 is slightly broader.
Both assert absence of numeral classifiers.
WALS 55A 'Optional' and GB057=1 both assert presence of numeral classifiers. Directional because WALS distinguishes optional vs obligatory; GB only marks presence.
WALS 55A 'Obligatory' implies GB057=1. Same directional caveat.
Both code presence of inclusive/exclusive distinction in first-person forms. GB028 explicitly includes pronouns and person indexes; WALS 39A targets independent pronouns.
Both assert absence of clusivity distinction.
WALS 41A 'Three-way contrast' and GB035=1 ('three or more distance contrasts in adnominal demonstratives') directly correspond.
Four-way implies three-or-more, so GB035=1 is a projection of both three-way and four-way values.
WALS 44A values with 3rd-person gender and GB030=1 both code gender distinctions in 3rd-person independent pronouns.
WALS 44A values with 3rd-person gender and GB030=1 both code gender distinctions in 3rd-person independent pronouns.
WALS 44A values with 3rd-person gender and GB030=1 both code gender distinctions in 3rd-person independent pronouns.
WALS 44A values with 3rd-person gender and GB030=1 both code gender distinctions in 3rd-person independent pronouns.
Both assert no gender distinction in independent pronouns.
Both assert no 2nd-person politeness distinction.
Both assert a 2nd-person politeness distinction.
Multiple distinctions implies presence of politeness marking.
Both assert no associative plural.
WALS 36A specific strategy values all imply GB046=1 (associative plural present). Directional: WALS preserves strategy subtype; GB only presence.
Same as above for periphrastic strategy.
Same as above.
Both WALS 63A and GB027=1 code that NP coordination 'and' and comitative 'with' are expressed by different elements.
WALS 118A 'Verbal' and GB068=1 both code predicative adjectives behaving like verbs.
WALS 118A 'Nonverbal' and GB068=0 both code non-verbal predicative adjective encoding. [polarity corrected: corrected polarity]
WALS 105A 'Double-object construction' and GB105=1 both mark recipient coded like transitive patient. Near-exact.
WALS 105A 'Indirect-object construction' implies GB105=0. Near-exact.
WALS 101A 'Optional pronouns in subject position' and GB522=1 ('pro-drop allowed') directly correspond.
Both assert mandatory overt subject pronouns.
Any WALS 71A value involving a special negative form maps to GB139=1.
Any WALS 71A value involving a special negative form maps to GB139=1.
Any WALS 71A value involving a special imperative form maps to GB139=1.
Both code a base-10 numeral system.
Both code a base-10 numeral system.
Both code a vigesimal (base-20) numeral system. Hybrid vigesimal-decimal also maps to GB335=1.
WALS 107A 'Passive present' and GB147=1 both assert presence of passive construction.
Both assert no passive construction.
Both code presence of morphological (affix/clitic) causative.
Both assert no morphological causative.
Both code exceed/surpass comparative strategy.
Both code locational comparative strategy.
Both code conjoined comparative strategy.
Both code particle/morpheme comparative strategy.
Both assert no possessive classifier system.
WALS 59A values with any classes imply GB058=1. WALS preserves class count; GB only presence.
Same directional logic.
Same directional logic.
